newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel recovers with fresh buying.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel recovers with fresh buying.

text.p: NWE high sulphur cracked fuel oil recovered some of the ground recently lost amid signs of fresh trader buying in the cargo market, dealers said.
High sulphur barges traded a few times at $99 and $100 fob ARA and the offer was later pegged at $110/$101, a rise of a dollar or two from Thursday.

High sulphur cargoes were firmer, too. One regular seller of high sulphur barrels said he saw a couple of new requirements from a trader who may be seeking to cover positions ahead of next week, when IP week industry functions in London are expected to stifle trade.
Russian high sulphur cargo premiums remained soft, however, as material continued to emerge apace from the Baltics.

An NWE refiner was thought to have bought at least three E-4 cargoes this week, containing around 1.5 percent water, at a premium of around $2-$2.50 to the mean/mean/mean of published quotes, and other refiners were also thought to have bought. Low water E-4 material was valued around $1-$1.50 more.
Traders felt premiums may remain soft amid a perception that crude oil futures may still have some way to fall.
Low sulphur fuel oil was around a dollar firmer.
